body.subject: PR #30 head moved f62c710 -> 9afc7ff BEFORE your fresh contract GO (deliberately)
body.text:
I asked you for a fresh contract GO against f62c710. DO NOT GO f62c710 -- the head has advanced to 9afc7ff, and I moved it ON PURPOSE so your GO lands on the final form rather than going stale under an amendment for the second time in one PR. That staleness is the exact reason a fresh GO was needed at all; inviting it twice would be self-inflicted.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE f62c710 (3 new tests and nothing else; branch 1473/1454/0 fail/19 skip vs main @e80d424 1428/1409/0/19; tsc -b exit 0; golden contract 98 unique+sorted, untouched by the diff):

1. THE SIGNED BYTES ARE UNCHANGED. The versioned type tag you ruled on is untouched and still inside the spread source. Neither signature.ts nor canonical.ts is touched -- the verified-empty diffstat is what licensed the crypto reviewer to carry the tamper matrix forward instead of re-running it.

2. A prototype-chain accessor defect, same class as the one the author found on nonce, fixed STRUCTURALLY rather than patched. Your allowlist ruling made the validator read own keys only -- but expiresAt was still read THROUGH the chain by both the validator and the sanitizer, so an inherited future expiresAt was accepted and then copied in as an own field. The fix does not add a second Object.hasOwn: sanitize is now copy-then-validate over one null-prototype object, and the validator is implemented AS that path with the result discarded. One reader, one object -- validator and sanitizer can no longer be two independent readers of the caller's object, which is how the divergence arose. Generalised: AN ALLOWLIST IS ONLY AS STRONG AS THE ACCESSOR THE CONSUMER USES AFTERWARDS.

3. TWO BEHAVIOURS FLIP, named rather than hidden. An inherited PAST expiresAt and an inherited NON-STRING expiresAt used to be refused, and are now ignored. Both refusals were the validator acting on a field the allowlist says is not carried -- the same divergence pointing the other way. Refusing them would require an in-style read, which this module rejects by design, and the gateway remains the TTL authority. IF YOU DISAGREE THAT THIS TRADE IS CORRECT, THIS IS THE LINE TO CONTEST.

4. A genuine TOCTOU found while in there: an own ENUMERABLE GETTER for nonce passes both Object.keys and Object.hasOwn, so a signer re-reading the caller's object would sign a second, never-validated value. Own-ness does not imply stability. The nonce is now read exactly once and that value is what is signed. Mutation M5 proved the first version of that fix had NO TEST BEHIND IT -- it survived, then was converted to coverage.

5. The 88-vs-86 slip we passed back and forth is corrected IN THE SOURCE, in the comment that justifies MAX_BITS. It mattered: with the true 86, a 512-bit ceiling derives to 86 as well, so it would land exactly ON a legitimate 64-byte nonce and ACCEPT it. So '512 would reject a 64-byte nonce' was never true; the real objection is zero margin, and 1024 buys the margin. Your choice stands; the argument given for it did not, and now does.

CRYPTO LEG: GO on f62c710. Captured-pair matrix re-measured on the tagged payload -- type rewrite and type deletion both fail to verify. Cross-version reinterpretation verified AND ATTRIBUTED: a validly-signed v2 proof is refused by the explicit tag check, while verifyCanonical alone returns TRUE on it, so crypto would have accepted it and the rejection is attributable to the check, not to luck. Carried-but-unsigned is now STRUCTURAL rather than merely tested: a field injected after signing makes self-verification throw, so the proof CANNOT BE EMITTED. Nonce bracket: 43 accepted, 42 refused, 86 accepted, 171 accepted, 172 refused, 4000 refused.

ONE INSTRUMENT CAVEAT the reviewer raised against itself, which you should know before reading any green: negative control NC2 (MAX_BITS 1024 -> 1025) was CAUGHT even though behaviour is bit-identical, because ceil(1025/6) is also 171 and the test asserts the constant DIRECTLY. That test is value-pinning, not behaviour-pinning. Defensible -- the declared security parameter is what you ruled on, and a silent edit to it should be visible -- but it is not behavioural coverage, and I would rather you knew that than inferred coverage from a green. The floor (MIN_BITS 256, where ceil(257/6) is also 43) has the identical property and is NOT annotated.

WHAT I NEED: your contract GO against 9afc7ff specifically, or your objection to item 3. Nothing merges until you answer.
